derivations.claim: If $V=\{0\}$, the identity $LT=I_U$ forces $U=\{0\}$ and $G$ has no eigenvalues, so the assertion holds with the stated zero-space norm convention. Assume henceforth $V\ne\{0\}$. Put $D=T^TAT$, which is SPD because $T$ is injective (if $Tu=0$, then $u=LT u=0$), and $C=LA^{-1}L^T$, which is SPD because $L$ is onto (it has right inverse $T$). Hence $G=CD$ is similar to the symmetric positive definite matrix $D^{1/2}CD^{1/2}$ and has positive real eigenvalues. For an eigenvector $u\ne0$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$, let $w=A^{-1}L^TDu$, so $Lw=Gu=\lambda u$ and $\|w\|_A^2=\langle Du,Gu\rangle=\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle$.

By [A1], $\langle Du,u\rangle=\langle Du,LTu\rangle=\langle Aw,Tu\rangle$. Cauchy–Schwarz in the $A$ inner product gives $\langle Du,u\rangle^2\le\|w\|_A^2\|Tu\|_A^2=\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle^2$. Dividing by the positive square gives $\lambda\ge1$.

Also $\|Gu\|_D^2=\|TLw\|_A^2\le\|TL\|_A^2\|w\|_A^2$. For the eigenvector, the left side is $\lambda^2\langle Du,u\rangle$ and step 1.1 makes the right side $\|TL\|_A^2\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle$. Divide by the positive factor to obtain $\lambda\le\|TL\|_A^2$.

Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and whose intersections are whole common sides, common vertices, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on the fixed polygon-shape, side-count, and shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

derivations.claim: If $a_i(v,v)=0$, each nonnegative term $\rho_i\int_K|\nabla v|^2$ is zero. Since $\nabla v$ is constant on each triangle, it vanishes on every triangle, so $v$ is constant there. Continuity across every shared edge makes neighboring constants equal; connectedness of the triangle adjacency graph makes $v$ one constant on all of $\Omega_i$. Conversely, a constant has zero gradient, hence lies in the kernel. This proves the floating-block nullspace claim.

A vector in the interior block's kernel defines a local $P_1$ function with zero boundary trace and zero energy. Step 1.1 makes it constant and the zero boundary trace makes that constant zero. Thus the interior quadratic form is strictly positive on every nonzero vector, so its symmetric matrix $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is positive definite. If there are no interior vertices, the unique map on the zero vector space is invertible.

If the global energy vanishes, step 1.1 applied triangle by triangle gives one constant on every subdomain. Interface continuity makes adjacent subdomain constants equal; connectedness propagates one constant through $\Omega$. The nonempty Dirichlet segment forces it to be zero. Hence only the zero global vector has zero quadratic energy, proving positive definiteness.

citations.quote: In the setting of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], the nullspace of the floating local energy matrix on a connected $\Omega_i$ is exactly the one-dimensional space of constants. The principal stiffness block $K_{II}^{(i)}$ on interior nodal values with zero boundary trace is positive definite (including the empty $0$-dimensional block convention). The assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

For each $i$, let $W_i$ be the vector space of local boundary nodal traces compatible with the fixed outer Dirichlet values, and set $W=\prod_i W_i$ (all interface copies independent). Let $\widehat W\subset W$ be the subspace whose nodal traces agree at every shared interface node; let $R:\widehat W\to W$ be the inclusion. Choose a set of **primal constraints**, meaning finitely many linear functionals on local traces whose values are required to agree across their incident subdomains. Vertex values and normalized edge averages are examples. The **partially assembled space** $\widetilde W$ is the subspace of $W$ satisfying those primal equalities, so $\widehat W\subset\widetilde W\subset W$.

The remaining continuity equations are collected in a jump map $B:\widetilde W\to\mathbb R^m$ with $\ker B=\widehat W$. It may contain redundant rows. Fix the **redundant-multiplier convention** $\Lambda:=\operatorname{range}B$ with its inherited Euclidean inner product: multiplier vectors are elements of this range, not arbitrary row-coordinate vectors modulo an unstated choice. Then $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$. For the PE26 two-dimensional estimate, all subdomain vertices are primal and the only remaining jump rows are nodal differences on open interface edges, each shared by exactly two subdomains.

An interface corner is primal whenever its value is among the selected primal functionals. An **edge average** on a side $E$ is $|E|^{-1}\int_E v_h\,ds$, which is a finite sum of nodal values for a $P_1$ trace. The two-dimensional bound below uses corner constraints; no edge-average bound is claimed there.

Use the interior/interface ordering of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]]. The boundary-trace spaces $W_i$, $W=\prod_iW_i$, the conforming space $\widehat W$, the partially assembled space $\widetilde W$, and the inclusion $R:\widehat W\to W$ are those of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]]. In particular, $R$ identifies the copies of a conforming interface trace. In subdomain $i$, write its stiffness matrix as

$$K_i=\begin{pmatrix}K_{II}^{(i)}&K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}\\K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}&K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}\end{pmatrix}.$$

By [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]], $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is positive definite when nonempty; on the zero-dimensional interior space its unique endomorphism is invertible. For admissible boundary trace $g_i$, the **discrete harmonic extension** is

$$H_i g_i:=\begin{pmatrix}-(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}g_i\\g_i\end{pmatrix}.$$

The local **interface Schur complement** is

$$S_i:=K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}.$$

This is the Schur complement in [[def-block-lu-factorisation]]. The local Schur form on a trace is $g_i^TS_i g_i$. The block identity and the associated block LU factorization use [[thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block]] with leading block $K_{II}^{(i)}$. Assembling local Schur forms on $\widehat W$ gives $\widehat S=R^T(\operatorname{diag}_i S_i)R$; restricting the same block-diagonal form to $\widetilde W$ gives the partially assembled operator $\widetilde S$.

derivations.claim: From [F3], block multiplication gives $K_iH_i g_i=(0,S_i g_i)^T$ and therefore $(H_i g_i)^TK_i(H_i g_i)=g_i^TS_i g_i$. Thus a zero local Schur energy is precisely zero energy of its harmonic lift. In a local dual subproblem the primal values are prescribed, so a zero-energy local vector, or the harmonic lift of a zero-energy dual trace, is constant by [F1]. A primal corner value is among its prescribed values; because the dual correction has zero primal values, that constant is zero. The local dual quadratic form therefore has trivial kernel and, being symmetric positive semidefinite, is positive definite.

For $g=(g_i)\in\widetilde W$, [F3] and step 1.1 give $g^T\widetilde Sg=\sum_i g_i^TS_i g_i=\sum_i(H_i g_i)^TK_i(H_i g_i)$. Each summand is a nonnegative local energy. If the partially assembled energy is zero, every summand is zero, so [F1] makes each local harmonic extension constant on its subdomain. Neighboring local constants agree at their shared primal corner. The adjacency graph is connected, so all constants agree; the global Dirichlet boundary makes the common value zero. Thus the partially assembled trace is zero, and its assembled energy matrix is positive definite.

The BDDC local dual solves use the positive local restrictions from step 1.1 and its coarse solve uses the positive partially assembled energy from step 2.1. The FETI-DP operator uses the same invertible partially assembled energy and the jump quotient of [F2]. Hence the exact local, coarse and dual systems named in the Statement are well-defined.

Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. $$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

derivations.claim: Let $f_i=(f_I^{(i)},f_\Gamma^{(i)})^T$ be local load contributions whose assembly is the chosen global Galerkin load vector, as specified above. The global interior rows are local to each subdomain and give $$u_I^{(i)}=(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}(f_I^{(i)}-K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}u_\Gamma^{(i)}).$$ The local interface residual contribution is $K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}u_I^{(i)}+K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}u_\Gamma^{(i)}-f_\Gamma^{(i)}$. Substituting the interior formula makes it $S_i u_\Gamma^{(i)}-(f_\Gamma^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}f_I^{(i)})$, precisely the local Schur contribution in [F3]. The global interface rows are the assembled sum of these contributions, not separate local interface equations.

Sum the reduced equations from step 1.1 over subdomains and identify copies of each shared nodal value as in [F1]. Because both the stiffness and the local load vectors assemble by summing their shared interface components, this gives the assembled interface Schur system with the correspondingly reduced global right-hand side. Any solution of the original global system yields this trace. Conversely, a solution of the assembled interface system and the uniquely defined interior values from step 1.1 satisfy every local interior equation and the assembled sum of interface equations, hence the assembled global system.

The global stiffness is positive definite by [F4], so the original solution is unique. Once the interface trace is solved, each local interior vector is exactly the reconstruction formula in step 1.1, which is unique because $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is invertible. Its trace-dependent homogeneous part is $H_i u_\Gamma^{(i)}$ from [F2]. Therefore static condensation is exact in both directions.

A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and whose intersections are whole common sides, common vertices, or empty. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. Assume the model of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], all subdomain vertices primal, and the coefficient-scaled average of [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Let $P:=I-R E_0$ be the complementary jump projection on $\widetilde W$, and let $\|\cdot\|_{\widetilde S}$ be the energy norm induced by the partially assembled Schur operator. Then

$$\|Pw\|_{\widetilde S}^2\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2\|w\|_{\widetilde S}^2\qquad(w\in\widetilde W),$$

where $C$ depends only on the polygon/mesh shape bounds and bounded side count. It is independent of coefficient jumps, mesh size, subdomain diameter, and subdomain count.

Let $A:V\to V'$ be symmetric positive definite on a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let $L:V\to U$, $T:U\to V$ satisfy $LT=I_U$. Every eigenvalue of

$$G=(LA^{-1}L^T)(T^TAT)$$

lies in $[1,\|TL\|_A^2]$, where $\|Q\|_A:=\sup_{v\ne0}\sqrt{\langle A Qv,Qv\rangle/\langle Av,v\rangle}$. When $V=\{0\}$, set $\|Q\|_A=0$ for its unique endomorphism. In that case $LT=I_U$ forces $U=\{0\}$, the spectrum of $G$ is empty, and the eigenvalue assertion is vacuous.

Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. In the two-subdomain edge case, its two entries are the coefficient-scaled jump weights complementary to those in $E_0$.

The **FETI-DP dual operator** and its preconditioner are

$$F:=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T:\Lambda\to\Lambda',\qquad M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}:=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T:\Lambda'\to\Lambda.$$

The multiplier convention removes dependent row coordinates: $\lambda$ is in $\operatorname{range}B$, so no arbitrary multiplier component in $\ker B^T$ is retained. Elimination of the partially assembled displacement and the resulting exact dual system are proved in [[prop-pe26-feti-dp-is-dual-schur-complement]].

For BDDC and FETI-DP built from the same positive definite partially assembled Schur operator, primal constraints, and scaled averaging, all eigenvalues of the two preconditioned operators other than $1$ agree with multiplicity. With the multiplier space fixed as $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$, neither operator has a zero eigenvalue; retaining all redundant row coordinates instead would add only multiplier null modes that are removed by this convention. The multiplicity of $1$ is not asserted to agree.

derivations.claim: Apply [F2] with $L=E_0$ and $T=R$. The BDDC eigenvalues are at least one and at most $\|RE_0\|_{\widetilde S}^2=\|I-P\|_{\widetilde S}^2$. By the triangle inequality for the induced operator norm, $\|I-P\|_{\widetilde S}\le1+\|P\|_{\widetilde S}\le1+C_0(1+\log(H/h))$. Since $1+\log(H/h)\ge1$, squaring yields the BDDC bound with a geometry-only constant.

Apply [F2] with $L=B$ and $T=B_D^T$. This bounds the eigenvalues of $F M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}$ below by one and above by $\|B_D^TB\|_{\widetilde S}^2=\|P\|_{\widetilde S}^2\le C_0^2(1+\log(H/h))^2$ by [F1] and [F4]. The Gram factors $F=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T$ and $M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T$ are positive definite: $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$ by [F4], $B_D^T$ is injective by $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$, and $\widetilde S$ is positive definite. Thus both maps are isomorphisms, and the stated product $M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}F$ has the same spectrum because $$F(M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}F)F^{-1}=F M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}.$$

Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and whose intersections are whole common sides, common vertices, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on the fixed polygon-shape, side-count, and shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

In the setting of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], the nullspace of the floating local energy matrix on a connected $\Omega_i$ is exactly the one-dimensional space of constants. The principal stiffness block $K_{II}^{(i)}$ on interior nodal values with zero boundary trace is positive definite (including the empty $0$-dimensional block convention). The assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

Assume the hypotheses of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and the energy setting of [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]]. If each floating local component has at least one primal vertex value fixed in its dual subproblem, its local dual stiffness is positive definite. If all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty, the partially assembled interface energy is positive definite; hence the BDDC and FETI-DP exact local and coarse solves are well-defined.

Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. In the two-subdomain edge case, its two entries are the coefficient-scaled jump weights complementary to those in $E_0$.

The **FETI-DP dual operator** and its preconditioner are

$$F:=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T:\Lambda\to\Lambda',\qquad M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}:=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T:\Lambda'\to\Lambda.$$

The multiplier convention removes dependent row coordinates: $\lambda$ is in $\operatorname{range}B$, so no arbitrary multiplier component in $\ker B^T$ is retained. Elimination of the partially assembled displacement and the resulting exact dual system are proved in [[prop-pe26-feti-dp-is-dual-schur-complement]].

For BDDC and FETI-DP built from the same positive definite partially assembled Schur operator, primal constraints, and scaled averaging, all eigenvalues of the two preconditioned operators other than $1$ agree with multiplicity. With the multiplier space fixed as $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$, neither operator has a zero eigenvalue; retaining all redundant row coordinates instead would add only multiplier null modes that are removed by this convention. The multiplicity of $1$ is not asserted to agree.

Then both preconditioned interface operators satisfy

$$\kappa(M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}\widehat S)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2,\qquad \kappa(M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}F)\le C(1+\log(H/h))^2.$$

The constant is independent of $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, and arbitrary positive jumps in the coefficient values $\rho_i$. If either preconditioned space is zero-dimensional, that interface solve is trivial and its condition number is not asserted. This statement does not cover three-dimensional vertex-only constraints, arbitrary graph or mesh geometries, or unaligned/intra-subdomain high-contrast coefficients.

derivations.claim: A dense Cholesky factorization of an $m\times m$ SPD matrix uses a constant multiple of $m^3$ arithmetic operations and stores $O(m^2)$ entries. Repeating on $N$ local matrices gives total $O(Nm^3)$ work, and perfect concurrency reduces the local phase to $O(m^3)$ time.

Since $n_c$ is proportional to $N$, dense coarse Cholesky uses $O(N^3)$ arithmetic and $O(N^2)$ storage. If $H/h$ stays fixed while the number of subdomains grows, [F1] leaves the iteration condition bound unchanged, but the coarse direct-solve work grows cubically.
